Thinking traps are habits of interpretation. Naming one creates an opportunity to check it.

## Thinking Traps {#thinking-traps}

### All-or-Nothing Thinking

Seeing a situation in absolute categories, with no middle ground: success or failure, perfect or ruined, best or worst.

### Overgeneralizing

Taking one event as proof of a broad, continuing pattern and using words such as *always*, *never*, or *everything*.

### Mental Filter

Focusing on one negative detail while filtering out other information that could change the overall picture.

### Disqualifying the Positive

Dismissing positive experiences as unimportant, accidental, or something that does not count.

### Mind Reading

Assuming you know what another person thinks without enough evidence.

### Fortune Telling

Predicting a negative outcome as though it were already certain.

### Magnification, Catastrophizing, and Minimization

Exaggerating danger, mistakes, or consequences while shrinking your strengths, options, or ability to cope.

### Emotional Reasoning

Treating a feeling as proof: *I feel afraid, so this must be dangerous* or *I feel guilty, so I must have done something wrong*.

### Should Statements

Using rigid rules about how you, other people, or the world must behave, then judging reality against those rules.

### Labelling

Turning a behaviour or mistake into a fixed global label about yourself or another person.

### Personalization

Taking excessive responsibility for an outcome or assuming another person's behaviour is about you when other explanations are possible.

### Overestimating Danger

Treating a threat as more likely or more severe than the evidence supports while underestimating available coping resources.

##### Automatic Thoughts

People at work don't believe that I'm really ill. They think I just want time off. It will be awful if people can tell that I'm anxious. People only care about themselves. I made a total fool of myself when I forgot his name. My friend is only calling because she wants something.

**I finally did some laundry today. But so what?**

Look at all the stuff I haven't done. I can't make time for myself because it feels selfish. I forgot about my son's baseball game. I'm a terrible mother. You should always try to do your best.
